release.title: NodeLink v0.1.4 Windows Update installation and accurate agent version reporting
release.intended_use: Limited pilot deployment to owned Windows x64 endpoints after the sole repository owner reviewed and accepted the release evidence; this release adds selective Windows Update installation (#51), tokenless in-place installer upgrades that preserve an existing enrollment (#178), heartbeat-reported agent versions with release binaries that must carry a build stamp (#179), and is not approved for multi-tenant or high-availability claims.

server.deployment: Deploy source from the exact commit bound to v0.1.4 by the release workflow.

database.migration_policy: Migrations are forward-only. 0029 adds the install_updates command kind to the commandkind enum and is additive; v0.1.3 databases upgrade in place from 0028. Public v0.1.1 databases must pass guarded schema adoption at 0001 before upgrading, and v0.1.2 databases upgrade from 0012; never edit a revision or perform an in-place downgrade.

protocols.mixed_version_behavior: Agents advertise command-v3 and command-v2 during a staged rollout, but new deployments require command-v3; missing, unknown, and legacy-unversioned capabilities fail closed. An agent that predates the install_updates command kind rejects it at kind validation rather than executing it, so a mixed-version fleet is safe. Heartbeats that omit agent_version are accepted and leave the stored version untouched, so v0.1.2 and v0.1.3 agents keep reporting normally until they are upgraded.

known_limitations: #24: Windows agent and installer artifacts are not Authenticode signed, so SmartScreen or antivirus warnings remain possible.
#66: Roles are global and clients or sites are not authorization tenants; do not market or operate this release as multi-tenant.
#84: Enrollment rate limits, counters, and metrics are process-local; no multi-worker or high-availability protection claim is made.
#126: Empty deployments must bootstrap the first client and site through the existing administrative API before using enrollment.
#76: The local release drill verifies the internal audit chain but has no external immutable audit-anchor receipt to cross-check.
Endpoint inventory, monitoring checks, alerting, and Windows Update scan/install are Windows-first; Linux and macOS remain development-only builds with reduced or absent collectors.
Alert email and signed webhook delivery are best-effort with process-local state; there is no multi-worker delivery deduplication or high-availability guarantee.

#61: the interactive shell remains a Phase-1 foundation only — the authorized, audited, capability-negotiated, time- and byte-bounded session lifecycle is implemented, but the live streaming transport, the agent shell I/O loop, and the terminal UI are deferred, so no shell session is usable end to end in this release.

#176: Windows Update installation is dispatched by explicit KB ID, Update GUID, or an install_all flag through the command pipeline; the dashboard does not yet offer a selectable update list, so operators select updates from the reported windows_updates inventory section themselves.

#179: an agent's reported version refreshes only on a successful authenticated heartbeat, so an endpoint that is offline, quarantined, or failing authentication continues to display its last recorded version.

This manifest's backup and rollback evidence is complete, but the full release drill's production HTTPS deployment and Windows canary phases are not part of these records and remain operator tasks before broad rollout.

prerequisites: Pause enrollment, command dispatch, scheduled-task execution, server promotion, and external agent rollout automation.
Verify the retained 0028 recovery point, a fresh pre-upgrade 0029-target backup, manifests, and retained restore evidence against their immutable SHA-256 digests.
Confirm Python 3.12, PostgreSQL, command signing keys, production secrets, trusted-proxy settings, HTTPS public URL, and server-only dashboard API URL are configured.

Verify every release artifact checksum and GitHub build-provenance attestation before execution, and confirm each agent binary reports 0.1.4 via `rmm-agent version -expect 0.1.4` rather than the unstamped 0.1.0-dev fallback.
steps: For a v0.1.3 database at 0028, take a verified backup, then run Alembic upgrade to 0029 and confirm the startup revision guard reports 0029 before serving traffic.
For a v0.1.2 database at 0012, upgrade forward through the 0013-0029 chain; for an unversioned public v0.1.1 database, run guarded adoption to 0001 first.
Deploy the server and dashboard together from the workflow-bound v0.1.4 source commit.
Deploy the checksum-verified Windows agent or installer to one owned canary endpoint before expanding the rollout; the installer upgrades an enrolled endpoint in place without an enrollment token.
Keep v0.1.3 and any failed-state backup unavailable to automatic rollout channels.
verification: Confirm Alembic current reports 0029 and health, readiness, metrics, login, and production configuration checks pass over verified HTTPS.

Confirm the upgraded canary endpoint keeps its agent ID and credentials, heartbeats successfully, and that the dashboard endpoint list and detail views report agent version 0.1.4 after that first heartbeat.

Confirm a scan_updates run reports the windows_updates inventory section and that an install_updates command installs only the explicitly selected KB IDs or Update GUIDs, with empty or ambiguous selection failing closed.
Confirm inventory snapshots, monitoring checks, alert state transitions, email/webhook delivery, script-library execution, and scheduled-task runs behave as expected on the Windows canary.

Confirm heartbeat, audit sequence including a single agent.version_changed event per upgraded endpoint, expected metric deltas, token revocation, agent revocation, and post-revocation authentication rejection.
Confirm NodeLinkAgent service and installer install, start, stop, restart, and uninstall behavior on Windows, with DPAPI-protected identity and restricted ACLs preserved across the in-place upgrade.

decision_path: Prefer a forward fix while the live database remains at 0029; 0029 is additive, so a v0.1.3 server generally runs against it, but that combination is not a verified release configuration.
Redeploy v0.1.3 components only when their required 0028 schema and retained artifact digests exactly match a restored deployment.
Before any schema restore, pause rollout and writers, preserve an encrypted failed-state backup, and name the decision maker and exact accepted data-loss window.

Restore the operator's own verified pre-upgrade 0028 recovery point only after explicit data-loss approval, validate it in isolation, and deploy the exact v0.1.3 server, agent, and installer together; the 0028 recovery point referenced below is the release drill's artifact, which proves the restore and decision procedure rather than standing in for that backup.
If the matching backup, artifact, audit, or startup verification fails, keep promotion blocked and continue with a reviewed forward fix.

security_impact.summary: v0.1.4 adds selective, explicitly targeted Windows Update installation through the signed command pipeline, makes in-place installer upgrades preserve the existing DPAPI-protected enrollment instead of re-enrolling, and makes each endpoint report its running agent version on every authenticated heartbeat so an operator can see what code an endpoint is actually running, while preserving fail-closed command verification, production configuration checks, and explicit pilot-only operating limits.
fixed_vulnerabilities: #179: agent versions previously froze at their enrollment-time value, so an operator could not tell which endpoints had actually received a security-relevant agent upgrade; the running version is now reported on every authenticated heartbeat, a change is recorded once in the audit chain with previous and current values, and a rollback to an older agent is surfaced rather than hidden.

#179: the release workflow and the installer compile now assert that each shipped binary carries its release version stamp, so an unstamped 0.1.0-dev development build can no longer be published as, or mistaken for, a release binary.

#178: in-place upgrades no longer request or rewrite enrollment material, removing the need to mint an additional enrollment token per upgraded endpoint and the risk of overwriting a token-free configuration; inconsistent or corrupt enrollment state blocks the upgrade before any file or service is modified.

#51: install_updates is role-gated, travels as a signed command envelope, and installs only explicitly named KB IDs or Update GUIDs (or an explicit install_all flag); empty or ambiguous selection fails closed, and an agent that predates the kind rejects it at kind validation.
new_risks: #24 remains open because Windows artifacts are unsigned and require checksum and provenance verification.
#66 remains open because authorization roles are global rather than tenant scoped.
#84 remains open because enrollment limiting and counters are process local.

Windows Update installation lets an authorized operator change endpoint state in a way that can require a reboot; restrict the operator role accordingly and prefer canary endpoints before fleet-wide installation.
A reported agent version is self-declared by the endpoint and is bounded, validated telemetry rather than an attestation; treat it as fleet inventory, not as proof of the running code.
operator_actions: Complete the production HTTPS deployment and Windows canary phases of the release drill and retain their evidence before broad rollout.

Because independent second-operator review is not available, the sole release operator must personally verify the complete v0.1.4 evidence index, retained digests, preflight result, and green release checks before tagging.
After upgrading a canary endpoint, confirm the dashboard reports agent version 0.1.4 for it before expanding the rollout, and investigate any endpoint that keeps reporting an older version.

Restrict install_updates dispatch to reviewed maintenance windows, and protect alert email and webhook secrets, single-use short-lived enrollment tokens, and reviewed script-library and scheduled-task content.
Use a forward fix by default; do not restore the 0028 recovery point without preserving failed state and explicitly accepting all post-backup data loss.
